svg.title: Illustrative AI-factory row: one 576-GPU unit of eight GB200 NVL72 racks with storage and three networks
svg.desc: Eight liquid-cooled NVL72 GPU racks, a coolant distribution unit, two switch racks and three all-flash storage racks sit in one row. A front-end Ethernet network runs above the row; a back-end compute fabric links only the GPU racks; a storage network links GPU racks to storage racks. A worked example shows storage at about 4 percent of row IT power.
svg.text: Illustrative AI-factory row: one 576-GPU unit (8 × GB200 NVL72)
Illustrative layout, not a vendor reference design. GPU-rack power is sourced; storage and switch rack power are assumptions.
Front-end network (Ethernet, north–south): tenant access, control plane, internet, dataset ingest
Storage network (Ethernet/RoCE): GPU nodes to storage racks; separate or converged with front-end
Back-end compute fabric (InfiniBand or Spectrum-X, east–west): GPU-to-GPU across racks
Worked example: IT power for this row
GPU racks: 8 × ~125 kW ≈ 1,000 kW (sourced range 120–130 kW)
Cooling, CDU and facility overhead excluded
NVLink: GPU-to-GPU inside each NVL72 rack (scale-up domain)
Back-end fabric: collective traffic between racks (scale-out)
Storage network: training reads, checkpoints, KV-cache spill
Front-end: tenant ingress, APIs, object ingest, management
Multi-tenancy is enforced on front-end and storage paths
Sources: NVL72 rack power ~120 kW (SemiAnalysis, 2024) and up to 130 kW (Gigabyte product page). Storage and switch rack power are
round-number assumptions for illustration; real values vary by vendor, drive count and NIC count. Not to scale.
